info.name: Tamagotchi Go - Game Workflows
info.description:
End-to-end game workflows that cross every service of Tamagotchi Go through the API Gateway.

| Folder | Story | Services |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Gateway entry and authorization | Gateway, User Management, Tamagotchi, Battle |
| 1 | Onboarding: players, package and pets | User Management, Package Registry, Tamagotchi, Notification |
| 2 | Social life and a PvP battle | User Management, Map, Tamagotchi, Package Registry, Battle, Notification |
| 3 | Guild life and a Monster Raid | User Management, Package Registry, Guild, Monster Raid, Tamagotchi, Notification |
| 4 | Resilience drills (manual) | Gateway, Tamagotchi |

Run the folders in order with the Collection Runner. Every run creates fresh players, so it can be
repeated on the same stack. Setup and required local values are in
`docs/game-workflows.md`. Never export or commit populated secrets or tokens.

exec: // One correlation id per call: the gateway forwards it and the services pass it on to every
// service-to-service call, so a whole workflow step can be traced in the logs.
// Trace any step with: docker compose logs api-gateway | grep <correlation id>

item.name: 0. Gateway entry and authorization
item.description:
The API Gateway is the only door into the system: it validates bearer
tokens against the User Management JWKS, removes `Authorization` and any identity headers the caller
sent, and forwards a verified identity (`X-Caller-Kind`, `X-User-ID` or `X-Service-Name`) instead.

Runs on its own: it registers a throwaway "probe" player. The service-token checks need
`battleClientSecret`.

item.name: 2. Social life and a PvP battle
item.description:
**Services:** User Management, Map, Tamagotchi, Package Registry, Battle, Notification.

Alice and Bob become friends and appear on each other's map; Carol, a stranger, shows up only within
6 m. Carol's pets become their secondary Tamagotchis, then Alice challenges Bob. The two players
take turns until one side is knocked out, and Battle settles the result through the gateway:
`Battle → User Management` (currency), `Battle → Tamagotchi` (combat profiles, XP, capture),
`Battle → Package Registry` (stat bonuses and boosts). Map reads relationships with `Map → User Management`.

Needs `mapClientSecret` and `battleClientSecret`. Run folder 1 first.

item.name: 3. Guild life and a Monster Raid
item.description:
**Services:** User Management, Package Registry, Guild, Monster Raid, Tamagotchi, Notification.

The raid administrator schedules a monster. Alice founds a guild that only players of her package can
join, invites Bob and opens the guild chat. Then the two of them take the monster down together.
Service-to-service calls: `Guild → User Management`, `Guild → Package Registry`,
`Monster Raid → Package Registry` (schedule and monster snapshot), `Monster Raid → Guild` (membership),
`Monster Raid → Tamagotchi` (combat profile, XP), `Monster Raid → User Management` (rewards).

Needs `adminEmail` / `adminPassword` (an account allow-listed in `PACKAGE_REGISTRY_ADMIN_USER_IDS`),
`guildClientSecret` and `monsterRaidClientSecret`. Run folders 1 and 2 first.

item.name: 4. Resilience drills: timeouts and concurrency
item.description:
Manual drills: arm each one with the Docker command in its description, send it,
then undo the command. Unarmed drills just report "not armed", so the Collection Runner can still
run the whole collection. The concurrency limits need parallel requests; docs/game-workflows.md
has a one-line shell command for those.

request.description:
1. `docker compose pause tamagotchi-db`
2. Send. The database never answers, so Tamagotchi's 4-second request deadline fires and it returns
   `504 REQUEST_TIMEOUT` in the shared error envelope.
3. `docker compose unpause tamagotchi-db`
